To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the development of emerging market bond markets is a process that involves both government and market actors, and that the outcome depends crucially on the pre existing structure and interests of market participants.
1. The development of domestic bond market in emerging economies is driven by the interaction of government and private sector actors.

(a) the main explanation for the variation in the development of bond markets is the pre existing financial structure; (b) the financial structure consists of a heterogeneous set of actors, interests, and influence constellations, which is the main determinant of the nature of market reform; (c) market reform in turn is the main determinant for the nature of bond markets that develop.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role that government and business actors play in the development of domestic debt markets, and the extent to which the development of domestic markets is driven by the government or by market forces.
the role of the state in the development of domestic capital markets in emerging economies, and with the interplay of state actors with private sector actors.
the question of how financial structure affects the development of domestic debt markets in emerging economies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of bond markets in emerging market economies has been driven by a combination of government and business interest.
financial structure matters, but not as much as one might have expected.
the development of domestic markets is a function of the structure of the financial system, the nature of the financial crisis and the political economy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
market development is not a simple matter of government policy but that government policy is constrained by the structure of financial markets.
financial structure, as defined here, is the main driver of market development, and that this development is not necessarily in line with government objectives.
the development of domestic corporate bond markets in emerging markets is driven by the interaction between the structure of the financial market and government intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of domestic markets is not a matter of policy, but rather a matter of financial structure.
the development of domestic debt markets is not a linear process, but rather one in which market development is contingent on the pre existing structure and the interests of market actors.

government efforts to promote market development can be successful in the long run, but only if the government can identify and work with the dominant actors in the existing market structure, rather than trying to create new ones.
